descs.t: Benjamin Netanyahu pushed for a strike on Iran before Israel's election on Tuesday, but President Trump refused, CNN reports, and Israeli outlets say IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir objected to the plan. CNN also reports Israel has suspended plans for more strikes on Iran in the immediate term. We walk through what is reported and what happens next.

Netanyahu says Israel has fresh intelligence that Iran will launch attacks to disrupt Tuesday's election, while reports say his army chief resisted a strike order and Trump said no. At the same time Trump issued a second endorsement of Netanyahu. We look at what this clash means for Israel's election and for pressure on the Iranian regime.

Netanyahu warns that Iran wants to disrupt Israel's election, and the fight over whether to strike the regime first has reached the top of Israel's army and President Trump. The Times of Israel and Haaretz carry the reports. We break down who said no, why, and what it means for the regime in Tehran.

intro.plain: Big news out of Israel. CNN says Netanyahu pushed for a strike on Iran before Tuesday's election and Trump refused. Israeli reports say the army chief, Eyal Zamir, objected too, and Israel has put further strikes on hold for now. Let's go through what is actually reported and what it means. Chat, should Israel have struck before the vote?
intro.mid: Netanyahu says Iran is planning attacks to disrupt Israel's election on Tuesday. Reports say he wanted to strike first, his army chief pushed back, and Trump said no, while also endorsing him a second time. Let's work out what this means for the election and for the regime. Chat, who do you think made the right call here?
intro.bold: Netanyahu says the regime in Tehran wants to disrupt Israel's election, and he wanted to hit it first. Reports say his army chief resisted and Trump said not now. So the regime gets a pause. Let's look at whether that pause helps anyone but Tehran. Chat, is holding back right now a mistake?

hook.plain: Netanyahu wanted to strike Iran before Tuesday's election. Trump refused, CNN says, and Israel's army chief objected. Here is what happened and what comes next.
hook.mid: Days before Israel votes, Netanyahu, his army chief and Trump split over a strike on Iran. Here is what that clash means for the election and for the regime.
hook.bold: Netanyahu says Iran wants to disrupt Israel's election. He wanted to hit the regime first, and he was told no. Here is who stopped it, and what it costs.

descs.t: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won reelection as Brazil's president, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff to secure a fourth term. Brazil's election authority put him at 51.76% with 99.8% of votes counted, after he came back from trailing. We walk through the result, Bolsonaro's refusal to concede and what comes next.

Flávio Bolsonaro says he will not recognise Brazil's election result and is asking the courts to annul it, after a Supreme Court justice extended voting by two hours. Lula da Silva's win gives him a fourth term, and analysts forecast a market plunge. We look at the extension, the legal challenge and how strong that case is.

Lula da Silva is back for a fourth term, and Brazil's right says the runoff was not fair. Critics point to a two hour voting extension ordered by a justice they say was Lula's former lawyer, while analysts forecast a market plunge. Here is what Bolsonaro is claiming, what the record shows, and why it matters beyond Brazil.

intro.plain: Brazil has a result. Lula da Silva won the runoff and a fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro after trailing. The election authority has him at 51.76% with almost every vote counted. Bolsonaro says he will not recognise it and wants it annulled. So chat, tell me: should a losing candidate ever refuse to concede a loss like this?
intro.mid: Lula da Silva just won a fourth term in Brazil, and the loser is not accepting it. Flávio Bolsonaro wants the result annulled, pointing at a two hour voting extension ordered by a Supreme Court justice. Analysts are already forecasting a market plunge. Chat, I want your read: is Bolsonaro's challenge about the rules, or about losing?
intro.bold: Brazil's left just held on. Lula da Silva is back for a fourth term, and Bolsonaro's camp is calling it stolen. Their target is a judge, reported to be Lula's former lawyer, who extended voting by two hours. Markets are bracing for a fall. Chat, straight question: if the right had done this, would anyone call it fair?

hook.plain: Lula da Silva has won a fourth term as Brazil's president, and Flávio Bolsonaro is refusing to concede. Here is how the runoff turned, and what his challenge can actually do.
hook.mid: A Supreme Court justice added two hours of voting. By the end of the night, Lula da Silva had a fourth term. Here is what Bolsonaro is challenging, and how strong that case really is.
hook.bold: Brazil's right says the runoff was stolen, and Flávio Bolsonaro wants it annulled. Before you pick a side, here is what the extension was, who ordered it, and what the numbers show.

descs.t: Nicki Minaj joined President Trump on stage at a Republican rally in Port Huron, Michigan, and pledged to support him again if he runs again. The rally was a push for Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race ahead of the midterms, as Fox News, the BBC and USA Today reported. We walk through what was said and why Michigan matters.

Trump brought Nicki Minaj to Michigan to fire up Republican voters for Mike Rogers, and told the crowd not to sleep through the midterms. Minaj said Trump has changed the energy of the country. We look at what this rally tells us about the Senate race and the Republican plan for turnout.

Trump went to Port Huron, Michigan, and said he was there to keep Abdul El-Sayed out of the US Senate. Nicki Minaj told him she would support him forever, and the father of Flight 93 hero Todd Beamer called on Michigan to vote red. We break down the rally and what it means for the midterms.

intro.plain: Trump was in Michigan, and he brought Nicki Minaj with him. At the rally in Port Huron she told him that if he runs again, she will support him again. The whole point was the Senate race, getting Republicans out for Mike Rogers before the midterms. Let's look at what was said and whether it can work. Chat, does celebrity support actually change how you vote?
intro.mid: Trump stood in Michigan and told Republicans not to sleep through the midterms, and next to him was Nicki Minaj saying he changed the energy of the country. This is a turnout play for Mike Rogers in the Senate race. Let's go through what it tells us about the Republican strategy. Chat, is Michigan going red this time?
intro.bold: Trump went to Michigan and said it plainly: he is there to keep Abdul El-Sayed out of the US Senate. Nicki Minaj told him she will support him forever and ever, and the father of a 9/11 hero told the crowd to vote red. Let's get into this rally. Chat, what does Michigan do in this Senate race?

hook.bold: Trump said he came to Michigan to keep Abdul El-Sayed out of the Senate. Then Nicki Minaj said forever and ever. Here is the rally, and what it means for the midterms.

descs.t: María Corina Machado, the Nobel laureate and leader of Venezuela's opposition, has returned home after nearly a year in exile to press for new elections, The New York Times and CNN report. Supporters lined the streets as she drove to Caracas. We walk through her return and what she is asking for.

Machado is back in Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile, and Marco Rubio says reconciliation talks made her safe return possible. Analysts warn the regime has made no concessions and the system behind it is still intact. We look at what her return changes for the opposition and the push for new elections.

After 10 months in exile, María Corina Machado stood back on Venezuelan soil and told her people: I am here. With you. Thousands lined the streets of Caracas. We break down her return, the fight for new elections, and what it means for a regime that still holds power.

intro.plain: María Corina Machado is back in Venezuela. The Nobel laureate and opposition leader returned after nearly a year in exile, and supporters lined the streets as she drove to Caracas. She is back to press for new elections. Let's look at what her return means. Chat, do you think Venezuela gets a real election this time?
intro.mid: Machado is home after more than 10 months in exile. Marco Rubio says talks made her safe return possible, but analysts warn the regime has given up nothing and its system is still standing. Let's go through what her return can actually change. Chat, is this a turning point or a show?
intro.bold: María Corina Machado walked back into Venezuela and said: I am here. With you. Ten months in exile, and now she is on the ground pushing for new elections while thousands fill the streets of Caracas. Let's talk about what this means for the regime. Chat, what should the opposition do next?

hook.plain: After nearly a year in exile, María Corina Machado is back in Venezuela and pressing for new elections. Here is how she returned and what she wants.

descs.t: Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets in France, and Fox News reports violent protests are now spreading beyond France as rioters clash with police. Reuters reports that Marine Le Pen has launched a presidential bid as the protests rattle the nation. We walk through what is happening in Paris, Orléans and beyond.

France's protests have turned violent in places, with clips from Paris showing police surrounded by rioters, and Reuters reports Le Pen has launched her presidential bid in the middle of it. We look at what this unrest means for France's politics and who stands to gain.

France is facing its biggest street unrest in years: hundreds of thousands protesting, rioters clashing with police, and the trouble spreading across Europe. In the middle of it, Le Pen has launched her run for president. We break down how France got here and what could come next.

intro.plain: France is on the streets. Hundreds of thousands are protesting, rioters are clashing with police, and reports say the unrest is spreading beyond France. And right in the middle of it, Marine Le Pen has launched her presidential bid. Let's go through what is happening and why. Chat, where are you watching from, and is it reaching your city?
intro.mid: France has a crisis on its streets. Huge protests, violent clashes in Paris and Orléans, and Le Pen choosing this exact moment to launch her run for president. Let's look at who gains from this chaos. Chat, does this hand Le Pen the presidency?
intro.bold: France is losing control of its streets. Hundreds of thousands protesting, police surrounded in Paris, riots spreading across Europe, and Le Pen stepping in to run for president. Let's get into what this means for France. Chat, is this the moment France changes direction?
